headline: State Park Camping and Pier Access Check
reservation: Oceanfront campsites at Myrtle Beach State Park and Huntington Beach State Park are the region's primary bottleneck, often booking 11 months in advance. While beach access is open, specific historical sites like Atalaya Castle require separate on-site admission. Always check the official South Carolina State Parks portal for current coastal access and camping availability.

days.title: Boardwalk and Pier Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Central Myrtle Beach

stops.name: Myrtle Beach Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the mile-long oceanfront promenade to see the SkyWheel and local landmarks.

stops.name: Second Avenue Pier
stops.detail: Visit one of the Grand Strand's historic piers for views of the Atlantic coastline.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for central town transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Paid parking is standard along the oceanfront; check local signage for rates.

days.title: Lowcountry Nature and History

stops.name: Huntington Beach State Park
stops.detail: Observe alligators and coastal birds along the causeway and visit the historic Atalaya Castle.

stops.name: Brookgreen Gardens
stops.detail: Explore the expansive sculpture gardens and wildlife habitats located across from the beach.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for travel to Murrells Inlet; conditions vary.
days.note: Insect repellent is highly suggested for the marsh boardwalks during humid months.

days.title: River and Maritime Forest

stops.name: Waccamaw Riverwalk
stops.detail: Experience the blackwater cypress swamps of the inland region along this scenic boardwalk.

stops.name: Myrtle Beach State Park Nature Center
stops.detail: Walk through the maritime forest to reach one of the last undeveloped beachfronts in the area.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for inland-to-coast transit; conditions vary.
days.note: The state park beach is significantly quieter than the central tourism district.

intel.title: Beach Access Fees
intel.text: Public beach access points in Myrtle Beach proper often use pay-by-phone apps. State Parks require a per-person or per-vehicle admission fee paid at the gate.

intel.title: Coastal Reliability
intel.text: Cellular coverage is excellent throughout the Grand Strand. Expect slightly weaker signals in the deep woods of Huntington Beach State Park.

intel.title: Urban Convenience
intel.text: Fuel stations are abundant along Highway 17 and Business 17. There are no gas stations located inside the state park boundaries.

intel.title: Tide Awareness
intel.text: Walking the beach is easiest at low tide when the sand is firm. Check daily tide charts if you plan to walk to the end of the piers.

intel.title: Rip Current Safety
intel.text: Always observe the colored flag system at lifeguard stands for daily water conditions. Beach access remains open year-round, but lifeguard services are seasonal.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Myrtle Beach International (MYR), pick up your vehicle, and head to your lodging in North Myrtle Beach or a State Park cabin.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is ideal; parking for large RVs is restricted in the central boardwalk area and requires specialized lots.
plan.goldenHour: Apache Pier for sunrise over the Atlantic; fog and humidity levels may affect visibility.
